label: late encoding phase + <DEL>, gated by first token (o/0/w/i/a/...) and by x/r/s/h/1/f/l-type inputs
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (encoding) phase from t>=3 and on the <DEL> step (98% of activation mass is in phase<=1, t>=3). It is silent at t=0-1 and almost silent in the copy phase (0.4% of mass, mostly recall_idx 1-2). Rate goes up with position in the sequence and with L. The <DEL> step has the highest single-step rate (15%) and holds 22% of the mass. Inside that window it is a soft, token-driven accumulator. It fires much more when the first original token is o, 0, w, i or a (about 3x lift; g, t, u give a weaker boost). Both the current input and earlier inputs being from {h, s, r, 3, k, f, x, 1, l, m, z} raise it; h is the strongest input token. It is mostly on first occurrences (in_first=1 holds 87% of mass), and the largest activations come late in long sequences on h/s/3 or <DEL>. Inputs such as j, d, n, p, v, q and first tokens outside the favoured set mostly keep it off. These weights are graded, not a crisp rule, so precision stays limited (about 0.44 dev) even though the phase/position window alone gives 0.96 recall.
